# Validates that the Docusaurus website builds successfully.
# Runs on PRs that modify website files or docs source files, and can also be
# called from other workflows or triggered manually.
name: "\U0001F3D7️ Build Website"

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      node_version:
        description: "Node.js version to use."
        required: false
        default: "24.x"
        type: string
      working_directory:
        description: "Path to the directory containing package.json (relative to the repository root)."
        required: false
        default: "website"
        type: string
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main"]
    paths:
      - "build/Update-CommandReference.ps1"
      - "build/eidsca/*.json"
      - "powershell/**"
      - "tests/**"
      - "website/**"
      - ".github/workflows/build-website.yaml"

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  detect-command-reference-changes:
    name: "Detect command reference changes"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      generate: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || steps.filter.outputs.command_reference == 'true' }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check command reference inputs
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d # v4.0.3
        with:
          filters: |
            command_reference:
              - "build/Update-CommandReference.ps1"
              - "powershell/**"
              - "tests/**"
              - ".github/workflows/build-website.yaml"

  generate-command-reference:
    name: "Generate command reference"
    needs: detect-command-reference-changes
    if: needs.detect-command-reference-changes.outputs.generate == 'true'
    runs-on: windows-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Generate command reference
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./build/Update-CommandReference.ps1

      - name: Package generated command reference
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ProgressPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
          $artifactRoot = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "generated-command-reference"
          $docsRoot = Join-Path $artifactRoot "docs"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $docsRoot -Force | Out-Null

          $sourceCommands = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "website/docs/commands"
          if (-not (Test-Path $sourceCommands)) {
            throw "Command reference docs were not generated at $sourceCommands."
          }

          Copy-Item -Path $sourceCommands -Destination $docsRoot -Recurse -Force

          $versionedDocsRoot = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "website/versioned_docs"
          if (Test-Path $versionedDocsRoot) {
            foreach ($versionFolder in Get-ChildItem $versionedDocsRoot -Directory) {
              $sourceVersionCommands = Join-Path $versionFolder.FullName "commands"
              if (Test-Path $sourceVersionCommands) {
                $targetVersionRoot = Join-Path $artifactRoot "versioned_docs/$($versionFolder.Name)"
                New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $targetVersionRoot -Force | Out-Null
                Copy-Item -Path $sourceVersionCommands -Destination $targetVersionRoot -Recurse -Force
              }
            }
          }

          Compress-Archive -Path (Join-Path $artifactRoot "*") -DestinationPath command-reference-docs.zip -Force

      - name: Upload generated command reference
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: generated-command-reference
          path: command-reference-docs.zip
          if-no-files-found: error

  build:
    name: "Build Docusaurus website \U0001F3D7️"
    needs: [detect-command-reference-changes, generate-command-reference]
    if: always() && needs.detect-command-reference-changes.result == 'success' && (needs.generate-command-reference.result == 'success' || needs.generate-command-reference.result == 'skipped')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: ⬇️ Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Full history so contributor profiles get display names and first-contribution dates from git.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download generated command reference
        if: needs.detect-command-reference-changes.outputs.generate == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: generated-command-reference
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/command-reference

      - name: Apply generated command reference
        if: needs.detect-command-reference-changes.outputs.generate == 'true'
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        run: |
          $ProgressPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
          Remove-Item -Path (Join-Path $env:WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY "docs/commands") -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

          $versionedDocsRoot = Join-Path $env:WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY "versioned_docs"
          if (Test-Path $versionedDocsRoot) {
            foreach ($versionFolder in Get-ChildItem $versionedDocsRoot -Directory) {
              Remove-Item -Path (Join-Path $versionFolder.FullName "commands") -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            }
          }

          Expand-Archive -Path "${{ runner.temp }}/command-reference/command-reference-docs.zip" -DestinationPath $env:WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY -Force

      - name: ⚙️ Set up Node.js ${{ inputs.node_version || '24.x' }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node_version || '24.x' }}
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}/package-lock.json

      - name: "\U0001F4E6 Install dependencies"
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        run: npm ci

      # The test docs are generated from the source module (Get-MtTest), which needs this module to import.
      # Without it the generator keeps the committed pages, so a PR's new or changed tests would not render.
      - name: Install Microsoft.Graph.Authentication for the test docs generator
        shell: pwsh
        run: Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Authentication -MinimumVersion 2.27.0 -Scope CurrentUser -Repository PSGallery -Force

      - name: "\U0001F3D7️ Build website"
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        env:
          # Lets the contributor generator resolve new commit emails to GitHub
          # handles (cached in website/contributors/email-aliases.json).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: npm run build

-    # Only versions with the module's major version share its commands: syncing 3.x pages into the 2.x docs

content.content:
- name: Generate command reference
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./build/Update-CommandReference.ps1

      - name: Package generated command reference
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ProgressPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
          $artifactRoot = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "generated-command-reference"
          $docsRoot = Join-Path $artifactRoot "docs"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $docsRoot -Force | Out-Null

          $sourceCommands = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "website/docs/commands"
          if (-not (Test-Path $sourceCommands)) {
            throw "Command reference docs were not generated at $sourceCommands."
          }

          Copy-Item -Path $sourceCommands -Destination $docsRoot -Recurse -Force

          Compress-Archive -Path (Join-Path $artifactRoot "*") -DestinationPath command-reference-docs.zip -Force

      - name: Upload generated command reference
      - name: Download generated command reference
        if: needs.detect-command-reference-changes.outputs.generate == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: generated-command-reference
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/command-reference

      - name: Apply generated command reference
        if: needs.detect-command-reference-changes.outputs.generate == 'true'
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        run: |
          $ProgressPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
          Remove-Item -Path (Join-Path $env:WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY "docs/commands") -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

          Expand-Archive -Path "${{ runner.temp }}/command-reference/command-reference-docs.zip" -DestinationPath $env:WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY -Force

      - name: ⚙️ Set up Node.js ${{ inputs.node_version || '24.x' }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node_version || '24.x' }}
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}/package-lock.json

      - name: "\U0001F4E6 Install dependencies"
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        run: npm ci

      # The test pages are built from the test catalog, exported from the source module (Get-MtTest), which needs
      # this module to import. Exporting it here means a PR's new or changed tests render in this build.
      - name: Install Microsoft.Graph.Authentication for the test catalog export
        shell: pwsh
        run: Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Authentication -MinimumVersion 2.27.0 -Scope CurrentUser -Repository PSGallery -Force

      - name: Export the test catalog
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        run: npm run export-catalog

      # npm run build also checks every URL in website/src/data/url-contract.txt against the output.
      - name: "\U0001F3D7️ Build website"
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: npm run build

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:

prefix: "chore(deps): "
    ignore:
      # Pinned to the oldest supported PowerShell: the engine compiles against it and the
      # runtime supplies the assembly, so a newer reference stops the DLL loading on 7.4.0.
      - dependency-name: "System.Management.Automation"

  - package-ecosystem: "npm"
    directory: "/website"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 10
    commit-message:
      prefix: "chore(deps): "
    ignore:
      # @docusaurus/theme-mermaid declares layout-elk ^0.1.9 as a peer, which allows
      # only 0.1.x, so 0.2.x (counted as a minor update) and 1.x break npm ci.
      # Lift once Docusaurus widens the peer range.
      - dependency-name: "@mermaid-js/layout-elk"
        update-types: ["version-update:semver-major", "version-update:semver-minor"]
    groups:
      docusaurus:
        patterns:
          - "@docusaurus/*"
      icons:
        patterns:
          - "@fortawesome/*"
          - "@iconify/*"
      minor-and-patch:
        update-types:
          - "minor"
          - "patch"
        exclude-patterns:
          - "@docusaurus/*"
          - "@fortawesome/*"
          - "@iconify/*"
          - "react"
          - "react-dom"

  - package-ecosystem: "npm"
    directory: "/report"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 10
    commit-message:
      prefix: "chore(deps): "
    ignore:
      instructions: |
        These command reference files are generated by `build/Update-CommandReference.ps1`.
        The generator sets `custom_edit_url` from a flattened `powershell/public/` base, so the URL does not always mirror the source file's nested folder on disk.
        Do not flag `custom_edit_url` as incorrect solely because the corresponding PowerShell source file lives in a subdirectory such as `powershell/public/run`, `powershell/public/services/entra`, or similar.
        Only raise an issue if the link is malformed, points outside this repository, or contradicts the generator logic.
    - path: "website/versioned_docs/**/commands/*.mdx"
      instructions: |
        These versioned command docs are generated artifacts copied from `website/docs/commands`.
        Apply the same rule for `custom_edit_url`: flattened `powershell/public/...` links are expected and should not be flagged as wrong just because the backing source file is stored in a nested folder.
  ],
  "ignoreWords": [
    "maester",
    "eidsca",
    "merill",
    "docusaurus",
    "devcontainers",
    "codespaces",
    "multifactor",
    "Dmarc",
    "Siem",

content.content:
## Contributing to Maester docs and blog posts

Simple edits can be made in the GitHub UI by selecting the `Edit this page` link at the bottom of each page or you can browse to the [docs](https://github.com/maester365/maester/tree/main/website/docs) folder on GitHub.

For more complex changes, you can fork the repository and submit a pull request.

The docs/commands folder is auto-generated based on the comments in the PowerShell cmdlets. If you want to update the documentation for a command, you will need to update the comment-based help in the .ps1 file for the command.

### Running documentation locally

The [Maester.dev](https://maester.dev) website is built using [Docusaurus](https://docusaurus.io/).

Follow this guide if you want to run the documentation locally and view changes in real-time.

#### Pre-requisites

[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) version 24.0 or above (which can be checked by running node -v). When installing Node.js, you are recommended to check all checkboxes related to dependencies.

#### Installation

When running the documentation for the first time, you will need to install the dependencies. This can be done by running the following command in ./website folder.

```shell
npm install
```

#### Starting the site

While in the ./website folder, run the following command to start the site locally. This will start a local server and open the site in your default browser to [http://localhost:3000/](http://localhost:3000/)

```shell
npm start
```

#### Editing content

You will now be able to edit add and edit markdown files in the ./website/docs folder and see the changes in real-time in your browser.

- Read the [markdown documentation](https://docusaurus.io/docs/markdown-features) for more information on some of the custom markdown features available.
- You can search for icons at [Iconify](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/) and include them in the markdown. See the [Daily Automation](https://maester.dev/docs/automation/) page for examples.
- The `Command Reference` section is auto-generated. To update the documentation for this, the .ps1 file for the command needs to be updated with comment-based documentation.

#### Blog post images

Every blog post has a card image (`img/card.png` in the post's folder) that is shown on the [blog](https://maester.dev/blog) and in link previews on social media. The images all use one template, so don't make one by hand.

You don't have to do anything: after a new post is merged, the `Blog card images` workflow makes its card and opens a pull request with it. If the post has no headline and label, Claude suggests them, and the maintainer checks them in that pull request.

To choose the text yourself, add a short headline and a label to the post's front matter:

```yaml

The Maester repository ships AI agents and skills that know its conventions: how a check is written,
which attributes it needs, how pull requests and issues are labelled. They work in
[GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/copilot) and [Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code)

cd /Users/merill/github/maester/.claude/worktrees/website-astro; python3 - <<'E'
p='website/docs/contributing.md'; s=open(p).read()
start=s.index("### Running documentation locally")
end=s.index("#### Blog post images")
new='''### Running documentation locally

The [Maester.dev](https://maester.dev) website is built with [Astro](https://astro.build) and [Starlight](https://starlight.astro.build).

#### Pre-requisites

[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) 22.22 or later (`node -v`). The CI builds use Node.js 24.

#### Installation

In the `./website` folder, install the dependencies:

```shell
npm install
```

#### Starting the site

While in the `./website` folder, start the site. It runs at [http://localhost:4321/](http://localhost:4321/) and reloads as you edit:

```shell
npm start
```

`npm run build` builds the whole site into `website/dist` and then checks that every URL the site has ever had still works (see [URLs](#urls) below).

#### Editing content

Guides are Markdown files in `./website/docs`. A file's path is its URL: `docs/monitoring/github.md` is
`https://maester.dev/docs/monitoring/github`, and a `readme.md` or `index.md` is its folder's page.

- Link to other pages by their file, such as `[Configuration](configuration/overview.md)`. The site turns these
  links into URLs, and they also work when you read the docs on GitHub.
- Notes and warnings use Starlight's syntax: `:::note`, `:::tip`, `:::caution` or `:::danger`, with an optional
  title in brackets (`:::tip[Before you start]`).
- A page that uses components (tabs, icons, explainers) is an `.mdx` file and imports them, for example
  `import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';` or
  `import IIcon from '@components/IIcon.astro';` for an [Iconify](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/) icon. See
  [Starlight's components](https://starlight.astro.build/components/using-components/).
- The pages under `Commands` are generated from each command's comment-based help: edit the `.ps1` file, not the page.
- The test pages are built from each test's `[MaesterTest]` attribute and `Test.<ID>.md`: edit those, not the
  website. `npm run export-catalog` refreshes `website/src/data/test-catalog.json` from your local tests (it needs
  PowerShell 7 and the `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` module).

#### Stable and preview

The docs describe the preview, which is published to the PowerShell Gallery each time a change is merged. Checks,
commands and parameters that the stable release doesn't have are marked **Preview** automatically, from the test
catalog and `website/src/data/versions.json`; you don't mark them yourself.

In a guide, wrap a section that only applies from the next release in `<Since version="3.1">`, or describe a change
in behaviour with `<Changed in="3.1">` (both from `@components/Since.astro`). The build compares the version with
`website/version-config.js` and shows **Preview 3.1** or **New in 3.1**; the release workflows keep both files up to
date. Write the docs in the same pull request as the change.

#### Explainers

Short animated explainers (in the intro and the applicability guide, and on the home page) are
[HyperFrames](https://hyperframes.heygen.com) compositions: HTML and CSS with a GSAP timeline, in
`website/public/explainers/<name>/index.html`. Their chapters and transcript are in `website/src/data/explainers.json`;
keep the two in step. Preview one with `npx hyperframes preview` in its folder. Each composition lists the source
files it describes (`Watches:` in its header comment). If your change alters what an explainer shows, such as a gate,
a reason code or a command's output, update the explainer in the same pull request.

#### URLs

`website/src/data/url-contract.txt` lists every URL the site had when it moved to Astro, and `npm run build` fails if
any of them no longer opens a page, directly or through a redirect in `website/src/lib/redirects.mjs`. When you move or
rename a page, add a redirect from its old URL.

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
E

[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) 22.22 or later (`node -v`). The CI builds use Node.js 24.

#### Installation

In the `./website` folder, install the dependencies:

```shell
npm install
```

#### Starting the site

While in the `./website` folder, start the site. It runs at [http://localhost:4321/](http://localhost:4321/) and reloads as you edit:

```shell
npm start
```

`npm run build` builds the whole site into `website/dist` and then checks that every URL the site has ever had still works (see [URLs](#urls) below).

#### Editing content

Guides are Markdown files in `./website/docs`. A file's path is its URL: `docs/monitoring/github.md` is
`https://maester.dev/docs/monitoring/github`, and a `readme.md` or `index.md` is its folder's page.

- Link to other pages by their file, such as `[Configuration](configuration/overview.md)`. The site turns these
  links into URLs, and they also work when you read the docs on GitHub.
- Notes and warnings use Starlight's syntax: `:::note`, `:::tip`, `:::caution` or `:::danger`, with an optional
  title in brackets (`:::tip[Before you start]`).
- A page that uses components (tabs, icons, explainers) is an `.mdx` file and imports them, for example
  `import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';` or
  `import IIcon from '@components/IIcon.astro';` for an [Iconify](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/) icon. See
  [Starlight's components](https://starlight.astro.build/components/using-components/).
- The pages under `Commands` are generated from each command's comment-based help: edit the `.ps1` file, not the page.
- The test pages are built from each test's `[MaesterTest]` attribute and `Test.<ID>.md`: edit those, not the
  website. `npm run export-catalog` refreshes `website/src/data/test-catalog.json` from your local tests (it needs
  PowerShell 7 and the `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` module).

#### Stable and preview

The docs describe the preview, which is published to the PowerShell Gallery each time a change is merged. Checks,
commands and parameters that the stable release doesn't have are marked **Preview** automatically, from the test
catalog and `website/src/data/versions.json`; you don't mark them yourself.

In a guide, wrap a section that only applies from the next release in `<Since version="3.1">`, or describe a change
in behaviour with `<Changed in="3.1">` (both from `@components/Since.astro`). The build compares the version with
`website/version-config.js` and shows **Preview 3.1** or **New in 3.1**; the release workflows keep both files up to
date. Write the docs in the same pull request as the change.

#### Explainers

Short animated explainers (in the intro and the applicability guide, and on the home page) are
[HyperFrames](https://hyperframes.heygen.com) compositions: HTML and CSS with a GSAP timeline, in
`website/public/explainers/<name>/index.html`. Their chapters and transcript are in `website/src/data/explainers.json`;
keep the two in step. Preview one with `npx hyperframes preview` in its folder. Each composition lists the source
files it describes (`Watches:` in its header comment). If your change alters what an explainer shows, such as a gate,
a reason code or a command's output, update the explainer in the same pull request.

#### URLs

`website/src/data/url-contract.txt` lists every URL the site had when it moved to Astro, and `npm run build` fails if
any of them no longer opens a page, directly or through a redirect in `website/src/lib/redirects.mjs`. When you move or
rename a page, add a redirect from its old URL.

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
E

content.content:
### Site versioning

There are two versions of the Maester website:

- [Production](https://maester.dev) - This is the live version of the site that is updated whenever a new version of the Maester module is released.
- [Preview](https://preview.maester.dev) - This is the version of the site that is updated with every commit to the main branch. This allows you to see changes before they are published to production.

| Environment | URL | Branch | Update Trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Production | [https://maester.dev](https://maester.dev) | website-prod | New Maester module release |
| Preview | [https://preview.maester.dev](https://preview.maester.dev) | main | Every commit to the main branch |

When a new version of the Maester module is released, the documentation will be updated to reflect the changes in that version.

#### Version numbers

A preview is a prerelease of the release it leads to, and the docs show that release's number.

| | Module on the PowerShell Gallery | Shown on the preview site |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Previews of 3.0 | `3.0.0-preview1` to `3.0.0-preview9`, then `3.0.0-rc01`, `3.0.0-rc02`, ... | `3.0.0-preview` |
| The release | `3.0.0` | `3.0.0` |
| Previews after it | `3.1.0-preview01`, `3.1.0-preview02`, ... | `3.1.0-preview` |

- A preview never uses up a release number, and every preview sorts below its release, so people on a preview are
  offered the release.
- The PowerShell Gallery compares prerelease labels as text, so the preview number has two digits: `preview10`
  sorts above `preview09` but below `preview9`. That is why the 3.0 previews after `preview9` are `rc01` and on.
- The numbers are worked out by `.github/workflows/Get-NextModuleVersion.ps1` from what is on the gallery. To start
  a new major version, raise `$major` in `.github/workflows/minor-version-update.ps1`.
- PowerShell installs `3.0.0-preview2` and `3.0.0` into the same folder. Someone who has a preview moves to the
  release with `Install-Module Maester -Force`; Maester tells them so when it starts.

#### Urgent changes to blog posts and documentation

If a blog post or doc change is urgent and cannot wait till the next release, create a PR against the `website-prod` branch directly.

Once that is reviewed and merged, you will need to create another PR to bring the changes into the `main` branch.

This is because the `website-prod` branch is deleted and recreated with every Maester module release to ensure it is always in sync with the released version of the module.

This process ensures any interim changes to the production site are intentional.

# maester.dev

The Maester website: the home page, the docs, the test catalog, the command reference and the blog. It is built with
[Astro](https://astro.build) and [Starlight](https://starlight.astro.build), and shares its design tokens with
[maester.cloud](https://maester.cloud).

```shell
npm install
npm start          # http://localhost:4321
npm run build      # builds dist/, then checks that every old URL still resolves
```

Node.js 22.22 or later. The contributing guide has the details: [Contributing to Maester docs](https://maester.dev/docs/contributing#contributing-to-maester-docs-and-blog-posts).

## Where things are

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/` | The guides and the command reference (`docs/commands`, generated by `build/Update-CommandReference.ps1`). A file's path is its URL. |

# Reminds a pull request's author when it changes a file that one of the website's explainers describes.
# Each explainer in website/public/explainers lists the files it watches in website/src/data/explainers.json.
# It only comments: an explainer can be updated in a follow-up.
name: Explainer reminder

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  remind:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      # The default branch's list of explainers, never the pull request's code.
      - name: Checkout explainer list
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: website/src/data/explainers.json
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Comment when a watched file changed
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          changed=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/files" --jq '.[].filename')
          message=$(node -e '
            const explainers = require("./website/src/data/explainers.json");
            const changed = process.argv[1].split("\n").filter(Boolean);
            const hits = [];
            for (const [slug, e] of Object.entries(explainers)) {
              const files = changed.filter((f) => e.watches.some((w) => (w.endsWith("/") ? f.startsWith(w) : f === w)));
              const touched = changed.some((f) => f.startsWith(`website/public/explainers/${slug}/`));
              if (files.length && !touched) hits.push(`- **${e.title}** (\`website/public/explainers/${slug}/\`) describes ${files.map((f) => `\`${f}\``).join(", ")}`);
            }
            if (hits.length) console.log(hits.join("\n"));
          ' "$changed")
          if [ -z "$message" ]; then exit 0; fi
          marker="<!-- explainer-reminder -->"
          body="$marker
          This pull request changes files that a website explainer describes:

          $message

          If the change alters what the explainer shows (a gate, a reason code, a command, a count), update its composition and its chapters in \`website/src/data/explainers.json\`. If it doesn't, no action is needed."
          existing=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR/comments" --jq ".[] | select(.body | startswith(\"$marker\")) | .id" | head -1)
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh api -X PATCH "repos/$REPO/issues/comments/$existing" -f body="$body" > /dev/null
          else
            gh pr comment "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
          fi

content.text:
The new maester.dev is built on Astro + Starlight. The build passes and every one of the 2,679 URLs from the old sitemap still resolves. Nothing is committed: the work is in a separate worktree, `.claude/worktrees/website-astro` on branch `feat/website-astro`, so your console branch is untouched. A local preview is running at http://localhost:4329.

**Preview by default.** The docs describe the 3.0 preview. A check or command that 2.3.0 doesn't have shows an "Only in the preview" box with `Install-Module Maester -AllowPrerelease` and links to the new [Get the preview](website/docs/preview.md) guide. That box shows whichever version the reader picks. The version picker in the header switches to "2.3.0 stable", and every mark then reads "Preview 3.0". Today that covers 192 checks, 22 commands and 16 new `Invoke-Maester` parameters. Guides can tag their own sections with `<Since version="3.1">` and `<Changed in="3.1">`.

**Keeping URLs and search ranking:**
- **No redirect hop:** every page is served at its URL without a trailing slash, matching the canonical tag and sitemap.
- **`/docs/next/*`** redirects to `/docs/*`.
- **2.3 command pages:** 659 redirect to the test that replaced them; 26 go to a frozen, noindex 2.x archive at `/docs/2.x`.
- **Build check:** `npm run build` fails if any URL in [url-contract.txt](website/src/data/url-contract.txt) stops resolving.

**What else is in it:**
- The home page from the mock: product tour, real counts, episode shelf, sponsors band with the CyberDrain and Increment logos.
- The faceted test catalog, with a copyable `Invoke-Maester` command for the current filters.
- Test pages built from one committed catalog file instead of 848 generated pages.
- Two HyperFrames explainers playing live with chapters and a transcript, plus a workflow that comments on a pull request when a change touches something an explainer describes.
- Copy page, a Markdown copy of every page, and `llms.txt`.
- The GitHub Actions, command reference generator, AGENTS.md, skills and contributing guide updated to match.

**Not done, or needs you:**
- **Cloudflare Pages settings** must change when this merges: output directory `dist` (was `build`), build command `npm run build`, Node 24. I couldn't confirm the current deploy settings from the repo.
- **The Xbox story** is in the code but hidden until you put a sign-off date in [media.json](website/src/data/media.json).
- **Also not built yet:** Sign in with ChatGPT, the docs MCP server, video renders of the explainers for YouTube, and per-page social images.
- **Repo files that still link to `/docs/next/...`** (README, pack guide) work through the redirect. I left them alone because some ship inside the module and packs.

**Tests:** 6,566 of 6,567 unit tests pass. The one failure is in the Zero Trust Assessment pack tests, and it fails the same way on a clean `main` checkout on this machine. It's not caused by this change; it looks like a side effect of version 3.1.0 of that module being installed here.

Maester 3.0 console output and performance work, done on PR 2334 (branch claude/maester-3-planning-6643a9) on 2026-10-10. Related: [[maester-3-design]].

Owner rulings (2026-10-10):
- Interactive mode prints no per-test lines at -Verbosity None, not even Failed/Error; live counts in the footer are fine "as long as it is reliable and not too many hacks".
- Keep the logo; improve it with colour for interactive runs (done: red-to-amber gradient, compact variant).
- Renderer is C# in Maester.Engine (MtConsoleRenderer).
- Perf fixes and the benchmark go in the same 3.0 PR, not separate PRs.
- Interactive runs take over the full screen with a dashboard (Copilot-CLI-style banner with the official flame, phases, product lanes, running tests); must work for future parallel runs and extra phases like data collection (as in the ZT Assessment).
- Product is a real [MaesterTest] property set on every built-in test (no parsing of Category); summary is a per-product table.
- Right-hand panels chosen by the owner: Tenant+connections, Failed by severity, Drift since last run, Pace/slowest, Blog, Version check, Tips; waffle chart of results under the lanes; user picks panels via Output.DashboardPanels. Tenant info can be absent (-SkipGraphConnect).
- CI annotations default was never ruled on; shipped on by default (cap 20, Output.CIAnnotations).

Later rulings the same day (these supersede the panel list above where they differ):
- Right column, in order: Tenant, Ring (results as a ring chart), Connections, Failed, Drift, Pace, Contributor (featured contributor), Blog, Tips. Version is not a panel: a newer version is a bold amber "↑ vX available" link under the logo.
- No extra Graph calls for the dashboard: the tenant object counts were built and then removed at the owner's request. Tenant shows name, primary domain, account only.
- Every panel should always be shown; Pace is the one that shrinks (chart + at least one test) and fills spare rows.
- Connections panel shows only which services are connected (no tenant names), connected first, alphabetical, Graph first.
- Featured contributor data is baked in at build (powershell/assets/ConsoleContributors.json via build/Update-ConsoleContributors.ps1); omit zero counts; people with pinLast are excluded.
- Status bar on the last row: wordmark gradient (owner disliked the pink/grey first version), full width, links left and right, a "⌘-click / Ctrl-click to open" hint. Owner declined mouse-tracking for one-click links after hearing the cost.
- Flame on the left of the wordmark, as on the site. No emoji in panels (terminals disagree on width).
- Layout (owner picked "option 4" after outside feedback that the logo took too much room): the big banner is only the opening screen while the run prepares; once tests start the header is one line (MAESTER in wordmark colours, version, phases). The Pace graph (one bar per test, scrolling, log scale, green-to-red rows) is in the main column between the product lanes and the result blocks. Right column in order: Tenant, Totals (stacked bar; the ring chart was tried and rejected as too blocky), Connections, Failed, Drift, Slowest (the flexible panel), Contributor, Blog, Tips.
- The owner wants mockups before layout or chart changes; show options, then build the one picked.

**Why:** the owner wants a richer TUI now that 3.0 is PowerShell 7 only, in the style of GitHub Copilot CLI.

**How to apply:** design lives in docs/proposals/maester-3.0-console-output.md; benchmark in build/perf/. Interactive runs must not use Write-Progress (its pane lands at the top of the screen in terminals that do not answer ESC[6n). The connection probe was measured at ~2.9 s (not 40 s; that was a stale Write-Progress line) and now skips EXO/Teams/PnP when their module is not imported; Azure and Azure DevOps still validate saved sign-ins over the network (~1.9 s). Open follow-ups: screen-reader detection, -DryRun still writes all reports, and (noticed 2026-10-11, not verified) the engine's "test run stopped early" error from Invoke-MtNativePlan is written while the dashboard is up and is not replayed afterwards. Warnings/errors shown after a dashboard run are only those from Write-Warning/Write-Error where the preference would show them (Get-MtDashboardMessageDefault); a default on every command replayed silenced noise such as '@odata.nextLink' cannot be found. On Windows the run switches the console to UTF-8 in Windows Terminal / VS Code only (verified by the owner on a Windows 11 VM); other Windows consoles get the ASCII fallback. My own working rule that cost me twice: read the test result before pushing, and never switch a checkout while a full suite is running in it.

**Console code review (2026-10-11):** two subagent reviews (C# renderer; PowerShell side) at 584c11d2. Fixed on PR 2334 in 58cc0497: untrusted text sanitised at the renderer boundary (PlainText / SgrOnly helpers in MtConsoleRenderer.cs; new setters must use them), hyperlinks https/file only, deferred warnings/errors after the dashboard, unknown-severity summary crash, console failures never fail a run, CI command injection in result lines, Get-Module -All in Test-MtModuleImported, terminal restore on failure and ProcessExit. Merill ruled: leave the redraw rework until the larger console changes he is bringing in; tracked with display-width measurement in maester365/maester#2361. To test the dashboard end to end without a terminal, run pwsh under a Python pty (pty.fork + TIOCSWINSZ 50x170); such runs are interactive and open the HTML report in the browser. A reviewer's full run with -SkipGraphConnect still used cached Azure and Azure DevOps sign-ins and made 48 read-only calls: use -SkipBuiltIn with a scratch custom test for no-tenant experiments.

**Design round 2026-10-18 (outlines + run progress):** Merill shared a reference video (Claude Code "opusplan tip" terminal animation) and liked its boxed panels, colours and dots running along connectors. Asked for outlines around the product lanes and running tests like the right-column panels, and an overall progress bar for the phases (Prepare, Run tests, Results, Reports). Mockups only so far, no code changed: artifact https://claude.ai/artifact/HYSY8R48JFLtGL882UbrFg (options: phases Today/Pipeline bar/Track/Boxed pipeline; outline Today/Separate boxes/One column/Coloured boxes; flow animation on/off). Merill's real pick (same day) was Track + Coloured boxes + flow on: I first built Boxed pipeline + Separate boxes from the recommended button he clicked, and he corrected it after trying it. Lesson: when a mockup page lets him choose, ask which combination he picked instead of trusting the default button. Track replaced the pipeline box (BuildTrack); Products box 38;5;71 green, Running 38;5;73 teal, Tests grey. Built on branch feat/console-boxed-sections (from main, not committed as of 2026-10-18): new MtConsoleRenderer.Sections.cs (BuildBoxedMain, pipeline, lane rows), plain layout kept below 34 content rows / 78 cols or when boxes would push out the insight panels (BuildBoxedMain returns null). Animation gated on Animate && Ansi && ticker, so event-only test frames stay deterministic. Mockup sources and a frame-dump script (calls the private BuildScreen via reflection with a StringWriter renderer, no tenant) were in the session scratchpad; the dump approach is the quick way to get a real frame without a pty.

input.prompt:
You are an expert technical SEO and web performance auditor. Do a critical, read-only audit of the rebuilt maester.dev website and return ranked findings. Do not edit any files.

## Context
- Maester is an open-source PowerShell framework that tests Microsoft 365 / Entra / Azure / Active Directory security configuration. maester.dev is its marketing site + docs + test catalog (~900 test pages) + command reference + blog.
- The site was just migrated from Docusaurus to Astro 7 + Starlight 0.42. Source: `/Users/merill/github/maester/.claude/worktrees/website-astro/website` (config `astro.config.mjs`, content loader `src/lib/content-loader.ts`, overrides `src/components/overrides/`, pages `src/pages/`, styles `src/styles/`). The built output is in `website/dist/` (build.format 'file': `docs/intro.html` is served at `/docs/intro`, no trailing slash). A preview server is running at http://localhost:4329 (use curl to fetch pages; do NOT use the Claude_Browser tools, another agent is using that pane).
- Hosting: Cloudflare Pages. `dist/_redirects` is generated by `src/lib/redirects.mjs`. `src/data/url-contract.txt` lists the 2,679 URLs from the old sitemap; `scripts/check-url-contract.mjs` verifies every one resolves. Don't re-verify that contract; it passes.
- Intentional decisions (don't flag as bugs, but do flag if implemented badly): docs default to describing the *preview* release; the 2.x docs live at `/docs/2.x/*` with noindex and are excluded from the sitemap; `/docs/sections/*` pages are noindex partials; old `/docs/next/*` URLs 301 to `/docs/*`; canonicals have no trailing slash; analytics are GTM + PostHog.

## What to check (be thorough, sample broadly across page types: home `/`, a guide `/docs/installation`, `/docs/intro`, test catalog `/docs/tests`, a test page like `/docs/tests/MT.1001` and a preview-only one like `/docs/tests/MT.1228`, a suite page `/docs/tests/cis`, a command page `/docs/commands/Invoke-Maester`, blog index `/blog` and a post `/blog/maester-3-0`, `/contributors`, `/contributors/merill`, `/sponsor`, `/manifesto`, `/test-builder`, 404)
- Titles (length, uniqueness, duplication like "X | Maester" patterns), meta descriptions (presence, length, duplicates across the ~1,200 pages; count duplicates in dist with a script), canonical correctness, robots meta, hreflang if relevant, Open Graph / Twitter tags (image, url, title), structured data (JSON-LD validity and appropriateness per page type: SoftwareApplication, TechArticle, BlogPosting, BreadcrumbList missing?), sitemap (dist/sitemap-index.xml, sitemap-0.xml: what's included/excluded, lastmod), robots.txt (exists?), llms.txt.
- Heading structure (single H1, logical order), internal linking (orphan pages, broken internal links — scan all dist HTML hrefs that start with `/` and check they resolve to a file in dist or a redirect in _redirects), anchor links, image alt text, link text quality.
- Performance: page weight per page type (HTML size, JS/CSS bundles in dist/_astro, largest assets, the big React islands, fonts), render-blocking resources, third-party scripts, image formats/sizes, the HyperFrames player bundle, Pagefind.
- Accessibility basics that affect SEO (lang attribute, landmark structure, contrast issues you can detect in CSS).
- Test pages specifically: are the ~900 test pages thin/duplicative? Titles like "MT.1001 - At least one ..." — good for search? Descriptions truncated awkwardly?
- Anything in the HTML that leaks build artifacts (".html" in URLs, localhost, broken canonical, etc.).

## Output
Return a ranked list (Critical / High / Medium / Low). For each finding: one-line title, evidence (URL or file:line, numbers), why it matters for search or users, and the concrete fix (file to change and how). Put the highest-impact issues first. Keep it under ~1,500 words; no preamble.

Test-page meta descriptions are raw, truncated markdown.** - Evidence: 875 of 899 test pages have a description of 299 to 300 characters ending in "…". Sign in to **Mic…", and bare URLs ("Learn more: https://learn.microsoft.com/…", MT.1001). MT.1025 to MT.1028 share an identical description starting `GET /beta/roleManagement/…`. For docs pages without one, fall back to the first paragraph in a `Head.astro` override (the 155-character helper from #3). Rewrite it as vanilla JS (a few lines) in `src/pages/index.astro`. - Home and `/docs/intro`: the HyperFrames Explainer script is 107 KB, and the `<hyperframes-player>` iframe (gsap 70 KB plus CSS) loads on page load. `Explainer.astro` imports the player eagerly. Switch to `await import('@hyperframes/player')` inside an IntersectionObserver, or add a poster that loads the player on click. - `/docs/intro`: the YouTube `<iframe>` has no `loading="lazy"`, and 17 other non-lazy iframes exist in the non-2.x docs (watch, monitoring pages, the maester-3-first-look post). It also includes 11 `/blog/authors/*` and 31 `/blog/tags/*` thin pages with generic descriptions. Either add `noindex` or filter them out of the sitemap in `astro.config.mjs`. The author pages have no internal links from page content (the only orphans besides `/`). **12. Blog posts carry two conflicting BlogPosting blocks.** - Evidence: `/blog/maester-3-0` has starlight-blog's complete block (author, Blog, BreadcrumbList) and the site's `Head.astro` block (no author, `.html` URL, no image). `/blog` also gets a TechArticle for a Blog collection page. - Fix: in `Head.astro` emit your JSON-LD only when the id does not start with `blog`. Add `image` and `dateModified` through starlight-blog. All 25 posts share one `og:image`, `maester-social-card.jpg`, although `scripts/blog-cards` exists. Set `image:` in the frontmatter of posts that have cards. **13. No BreadcrumbList or page-type structured data on docs, tests or commands.** - Evidence: test pages, command pages and docs are generic `TechArticle` with no author or dates. - Fix: in `Head.astro`, emit BreadcrumbList (Docs > Test catalog > CIS > ID). For tests, add `about` pointing at the product. Contributor pages could be `ProfilePage`/`Person` (they currently have none). The home page could add `WebSite` and `Organization`. `SoftwareApplication` is fine, but it won't get a rich result without rating data. **14. Test pages are weakly linked and partly boilerplate.** - Evidence: the `<main>` of `MT.1001` links only to the `.md` copy, ChatGPT/Claude prompts, `/llms.txt`, contributors, Learn, GitHub and `/sponsor`. GTM loads on every host and has no consent gate.** - Evidence: `src/components/Analytics.astro` says "maester.dev only" but only PostHog checks `location.hostname`. GTM loads on previews, `*.pages.dev` and localhost, and sends hits from them. There is no `<noscript>` GTM fallback. - Fix: wrap the GTM block in the same hostname check. **20. Five `/docs/sections/*` pages link to their own `.md`, which is not generated for sections. Three links have trailing slashes: `/docs/tests/` (×2), `/docs/tests/cis/` and `/docs/tests/eidsca/`. 40 links point at redirect sources, such as `/blog/authors/sebastian` and `/docs/commands/Test-MtAd*CaCount`; fix them at source. - **Edit-this-page on generated pages 404s.** `https://github.com/maester365/maester/edit/main/website/.generated/tests/maester/MT.1001.md` does not exist on GitHub. Point it at the source test `.md` in `tests/<suite>/…` and hide it for commands. - **llms files.** `llms.txt` has only two links and no page index. `llms-full.txt` is 7.3 MB and `llms-small.txt` is 4.1 MB; the "small" one still contains all 888 test pages. Exclude `docs/tests/**` from the small file (`exclude` in the `starlightLlmsTxt` config) and list the main sections in `llms.txt`. - **Duplicate H1 and heading skips.** MT.1066 and MT.1067 and 3 command pages (Get-MtUserAuthenticationMethod and similar) have two H1s (the title plus a `# ` in the source). About 836 pages go from H2 to H4 ("Remediation action", "Control Type"): in the generator use `###`. The footer uses `<h2>` for link groups (Product, Docs…) on every custom page, and `<script type="module">` is emitted after `</html>` on the home page. - **Social tags.** `og:type=article` is used on listing pages (blog index, suites, 404). There is no `twitter:image:alt` or `og:image:width/height`, no `article:published_time` on blog posts, and no `apple-touch-icon`. `<meta name="keywords">` on test pages is ignored by Google; drop it. - **Fonts.** There is no `<link rel="preload">` for the latin Inter and Geist Mono woff2, which are discovered late through the CSS. Font-display is `swap`. Self-hosted, 10 woff plus 13 woff2 files are shipped, but only the matching subsets download. - **Contrast.** In dark mode, `--sl-color-gray-4` (#71717a) on #18181b is 3.7:1, which fails AA for text. It is only defined for borders and Docusaurus-compat variables. Other pairs checked pass: gray-4 on #fafafa is 4.6:1, and the accent is 7.2:1 dark and 5.1:1 light. - **`/docs/tests` is 777 KB HTML (71 KB gzip) with about 1,789 table rows.** It is acceptable, but a large DOM. Consider rendering per-suite tables on the suite pages and filtering client-side. - **Redirect chains.** `/docs/next/commands/Test-Azdo…` goes to `/docs/commands/Test-Azdo…`, which goes to `/docs/tests/AZDO.xxxx`. Resolve these in `src/lib/redirects.mjs` so the `/docs/next/*` entries go straight to the final target. ## Checked and fine - Canonicals match each page's URL: 0 mismatches, none with trailing slashes or `.html`. - `og:url` equals the canonical everywhere. - `lang="en"` is set on all pages. - Every `<img>` has an `alt` attribute (99 are intentionally empty). - No empty or "click here" links. - noindex is applied to 131 pages (2.x and sections) plus `/demo/report`. - The sitemap excludes 2.x and sections, and no `.html`, localhost or trailing-slash URLs appear in it. - A single H1 appears on every Starlight page (apart from the exceptions above), and landmarks are present. - The RSS feed exists at `/blog/rss.xml`. - The 128 pages with identical descriptions drop to 11 groups (103 pages) once 2.x is excluded: 81 pages with the generic description (#4) plus the near-identical test-page pairs. Duplicate titles drop to 5 groups (10 pages): the "Overview", "Connect-Maester", "Azure DevOps", "Azure Automation" and "Blog | Maester" titles. - The Mermaid, ELK, KaTeX and Cytoscape bundles in `_astro` are only pulled on pages that use them (the largest is `elk` at 1.4 MB). Based on `website/dist/` as rebuilt at 18:27 (1,312 HTML files, 1,180 indexable, 1,177 in the sitemap) and the preview server at localhost:4329. ## Critical **1. Every sidebar, prev/next and logo link ends in `.html`.** - Evidence: 36,602 `href="….html"` links across the built pages. Every page has the logo link `/index.html`; every test page has nine suite links such as `/docs/tests/cis.html`; docs pages link `/docs/installation.html`, `/docs/intro.html` and so on. `dist/docs/installation.html` has 50 `.html` links against 37 clean ones. Prev/next is ``. - Why it matters: Starlight appends `.html` when `build.format` is `'file'`. Cloudflare Pages answers `/x.html` with a 308 to `/x`, so every sidebar click costs a redirect hop. Crawlers see non-canonical internal links on every page, which wastes crawl budget and dilutes link signals. The URL contract check doesn't catch it because the files exist. - Fix: add a small integration in `astro.config.mjs` using the `astro:build:done` hook. It rewrites internal `href="/…​.html"` to the clean path (and `/index.html` to `/`) in `dist/**/*.html`, skipping `/explainers/` and `/demo/`. Or drop the `.html` in a `Sidebar.astro`/`PageFrame` override plus a postbuild script. **2. JSON-LD URLs contain `.html` on every Starlight page.** - Evidence: `/docs/tests/MT.1001` has `"url":"https://maester.dev/docs/tests/MT.1001.html"`. Same on `/docs/installation`, `/blog.html`, `/404.html`, and both blog-post blocks (`/blog/maester-3-0.html`). The cause is `new URL(Astro.url.pathname, Astro.site)` in `src/components/overrides/Head.astro:11`, because the pathname includes `.html` under format 'file'. - Why it matters: the structured data contradicts the canonical, on about 1,150 pages. - Fix: in `Head.astro`, use `Astro.locals.starlightRoute.head` canonical or `Astro.url.pathname.replace(/\.html$/, '')`. The same bug sits in the VideoObject `embedUrl` (`/explainers/run/index.html`) on the home page. **3. Test-page meta descriptions are raw, truncated markdown.** - Evidence: 875 of 899 test pages have a description of 299 to 300 characters ending in "…". Google shows about 155. 422 contain markdown or table syntax: `**assigned**`, backticks, `- Organizational Units…` (AD-OU-03), "Remediation action 1. Sign in to **Mic…", and bare URLs ("Learn more: https://learn.microsoft.com/…", MT.1001). MT.1025 to MT.1028 share an identical description starting `GET /beta/roleManagement/…`. Some CISA and ORCA pairs are identical (ORCA.120.1/.3, CISA.MS.EXO.9.2/.9.3, CISA.MS.AAD.7.8/.7.9, MT.1003/.1004). - Why it matters: this is the snippet users see in search results for about 900 pages. - Fix: `trimDescription()` in `website/scripts/generate-test-docs.mjs:184`. Strip `**`, backticks, list markers, bare URLs and anything from "Remediation action" onward. Cut at the last sentence or word boundary at or below 155 characters. If the result is under 70 characters, append the product and feature ("Checks … in Intune compliance policies."). That also removes the duplicates. ## High **4. 81 indexable pages have the generic site description.** - Evidence: "Open-source security testing for Microsoft 365…" is the description on `/docs/intro`, `/docs/installation`, `/docs/faq`, `/docs/connect-maester`, `/docs/monitoring/*` (14 pages), `/docs/alerts/*`, `/docs/multi-tenant/*`, `/docs/writing-tests/*`, `/blog` and `/blog/2`, `/blog/tags/*`, `/blog/authors/*`, and `/404`. - Why it matters: the highest-value pages share one snippet. - Fix: add `description:` to those pages' frontmatter. For docs pages without one, fall back to the first paragraph in a `Head.astro` override (the 155-character helper from #3). For `/blog` and `/blog/2`, give the page-specific title and description through starlight-blog config. **5. No `robots.txt`.** - Evidence: `public/` has no `robots.txt` (`curl /robots.txt` returns the 404 page) and no `_headers` file. The old site had none either. - Fix: add `public/robots.txt` with `User-agent: *`, `Allow: /` and `Sitemap: https://maester.dev/sitemap-index.xml`. Do not Disallow `/docs/2.x` or `/docs/sections`, because Google must be able to fetch the page to see its noindex. Disallowing `/explainers/` is fine. **6. Test titles are long and put the ID before the meaning.** - Evidence: 823 of 1,180 indexable titles are over 60 characters, 184 are over 100, and the longest is 208 (CISA.MS.EXO.8.4). 433 of 891 test pages end the title with ".", for example "MT.1001 - At least one … device compliance. | Maester". - Why it matters: titles are truncated in results and the key phrase can get cut off. - Fix: in `generate-test-docs.mjs` (around line 519), strip the trailing period and use ` (MT.1001)`, with an explicit `head` title of `<Title (≤ 55 chars)> (ID) | Maester` for long ones. Keep the H1 as it is. **7. `/manifesto` has no H1.** - Evidence: `<main>` starts with a `<p>`. `remarkStripTitle` is registered globally in `astro.config.mjs`, so it strips the `# The Maester Manifesto` from `src/pages/manifesto.md` and the layout never adds it back. - Fix: render `<h1>{title}</h1>` in `src/layouts/MarkdownPage.astro`, or skip the strip plugin for `src/pages/**`. **8. Nested `<main>` on `/contributors`, `/sponsor` and 74 `/contributors/*` pages.** - Evidence: the layout emits `<main id="main" class="site-main">` and the React page component emits a second `<main class="_page_1j3kw_1">`. `dist/contributors/blindzero.html` has 2. - Why it matters: invalid HTML with two main landmarks. - Fix: change the inner element to `<div>` in the `src/components/Contributors*` and `Sponsor*` components. **9. The 11.4 MB `dist/img/maester-demo.gif` is orphaned.** - Evidence: it is not referenced by any built HTML, but `public/img/maester-demo.gif` ships to Cloudflare. - Fix: check external references (README, PSGallery). If none, delete it. Otherwise convert it to mp4/webp. **10. Home page and `/docs/intro` load more than they need above the fold.** - Home: the `PronunciationButton` is a React island (`client:visible`), so `client.js` (205 KB, 65 KB gzip) plus React load for one button. Rewrite it as vanilla JS (a few lines) in `src/pages/index.astro`. - Home and `/docs/intro`: the HyperFrames Explainer script is 107 KB, and the `<hyperframes-player>` iframe (gsap 70 KB plus CSS) loads on page load. `Explainer.astro` imports the player eagerly. Switch to `await import('@hyperframes/player')` inside an IntersectionObserver, or add a poster that loads the player on click. - `/docs/intro`: the YouTube `<iframe>` has no `loading="lazy"`, and 17 other non-lazy iframes exist in the non-2.x docs (watch, monitoring pages, the maester-3-first-look post). Fix with a remark/rehype plugin that adds `loading="lazy"` to iframes. ## Medium **11. Sitemap has no `<lastmod>` (0 of 1,177 entries).** - Fix: in the `sitemap({...})` config add `serialize`, using the blog `date` for posts and the build date for everything else, or git dates for docs. It also includes 11 `/blog/authors/*` and 31 `/blog/tags/*` thin pages with generic descriptions. Either add `noindex` or filter them out of the sitemap in `astro.config.mjs`. The author pages have no internal links from page content (the only orphans besides `/`). **12. Blog posts carry two conflicting BlogPosting blocks.** - Evidence: `/blog/maester-3-0` has starlight-blog's complete block (author, Blog, BreadcrumbList) and the site's `Head.astro` block (no author, `.html` URL, no image). `/blog` also gets a TechArticle for a Blog collection page. - Fix: in `Head.astro` emit your JSON-LD only when the id does not start with `blog`. Add `image` and `dateModified` through starlight-blog. All 25 posts share one `og:image`, `maester-social-card.jpg`, although `scripts/blog-cards` exists. Set `image:` in the frontmatter of posts that have cards. **13. No BreadcrumbList or page-type structured data on docs, tests or commands.** - Evidence: test pages, command pages and docs are generic `TechArticle` with no author or dates. - Fix: in `Head.astro`, emit BreadcrumbList (Docs > Test catalog > CIS > ID). For tests, add `about` pointing at the product. Contributor pages could be `ProfilePage`/`Person` (they currently have none). The home page could add `WebSite` and `Organization`. `SoftwareApplication` is fine, but it won't get a rich result without rating data. **14. Test pages are weakly linked and partly boilerplate.** - Evidence: the `<main>` of `MT.1001` links only to the `.md` copy, ChatGPT/Claude prompts, `/llms.txt`, contributors, Learn, GitHub and `/sponsor`. There is no link to its suite page, the catalog, the product or related tests, and no breadcrumb. 17 pages still say "Review the configuration described above." Median body is 255 words for MT, 421 for CIS and about 175 to 215 for ORCA/AD/EIDSCA. That is thin but unique, not duplicated. - Fix: in `generate-test-docs.mjs`, add a "Part of: Suite · Product · Feature" line linking `/docs/tests/<suite>` and a related-tests list, and render the breadcrumbs. Replace or drop the boilerplate remediation text. **15. The `/docs/**/*.md` mirrors are crawlable.** - Evidence: 1,030 `.md` files are served as `text/markdown`, and every docs page links to its own, so they can be indexed as duplicates. - Fix: add `public/_headers` with `/*.md` and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, plus `Link: <canonical>; rel="canonical"` if wanted. **16. No cache headers.** - Evidence: there is no `public/_headers`, so Cloudflare serves `max-age=0, must-revalidate`, including for the 19 MB of hashed `_astro/*`, the fonts and the 14 MB of `img/`. - Fix: in `public/_headers`, set `/_astro/*` to `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and `/img/*` to one week or more. Add basic security headers. **17. Explainer pages are crawlable but incomplete.** - Evidence: `/explainers/run/` and `/explainers/gates/` have no `<title>`, description, canonical or robots tag. - Fix: add `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` and a title in the composition template (`scripts/copy-explainer-assets.mjs` source). The VideoObject on the home page and `/docs/intro` has an `uploadDate` equal to the build date and an `embedUrl` that is a composition HTML, not a player. It is unlikely to produce a rich result and could mislead; use real values or drop it. **18. 1,859 pages hotlink GitHub avatars.** - Evidence: `<img src="https://github.com/merill.png" alt="…">` with no width/height. It is a 302 per avatar and a third-party host. 974 pages have images without dimensions, including 105 on `/contributors` and 23 on `/sponsor`. The home page also hotlinks about 22 avatars (lazy, with dimensions). - Fix: in `generate-test-docs.mjs`, add `width="28" height="28"` and `loading="lazy" decoding="async"`, and ideally use `avatars.githubusercontent.com/<id>?s=56` or self-host. **19. GTM loads on every host and has no consent gate.** - Evidence: `src/components/Analytics.astro` says "maester.dev only" but only PostHog checks `location.hostname`. GTM loads on previews, `*.pages.dev` and localhost, and sends hits from them. There is no `<noscript>` GTM fallback. - Fix: wrap the GTM block in the same hostname check. **20. Pagefind indexes pages that aren't in search scope.** - Evidence: 1,184 pages are indexed, including the 126 2.x pages and 5 `/docs/sections/*` partials, so search results show 2.x pages. - Fix: set `pagefind: false` in frontmatter for 2.x and sections, or put `data-pagefind-ignore` in the page template for those ids. The index is 7.2 MB (on demand, so fine). ## Low - **Broken internal links, 7 of about 73k scanned.** `/docs/connect-maester` links to `/docs/tests/maester/MT.1076` (should be `/docs/tests/MT.1076`). `/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric` links to `/docs/tests/eidsca/EIDSCA.AP14` (should be `/docs/tests/EIDSCA.AP14`). Five `/docs/sections/*` pages link to their own `.md`, which is not generated for sections. Three links have trailing slashes: `/docs/tests/` (×2), `/docs/tests/cis/` and `/docs/tests/eidsca/`. 40 links point at redirect sources, such as `/blog/authors/sebastian` and `/docs/commands/Test-MtAd*CaCount`; fix them at source. - **Edit-this-page on generated pages 404s.** `https://github.com/maester365/maester/edit/main/website/.generated/tests/maester/MT.1001.md` does not exist on GitHub. Point it at the source test `.md` in `tests/<suite>/…` and hide it for commands. - **llms files.** `llms.txt` has only two links and no page index. `llms-full.txt` is 7.3 MB and `llms-small.txt` is 4.1 MB; the "small" one still contains all 888 test pages. Exclude `docs/tests/**` from the small file (`exclude` in the `starlightLlmsTxt` config) and list the main sections in `llms.txt`. - **Duplicate H1 and heading skips.** MT.1066 and MT.1067 and 3 command pages (Get-MtUserAuthenticationMethod and similar) have two H1s (the title plus a `# ` in the source). About 836 pages go from H2 to H4 ("Remediation action", "Control Type"): in the generator use `###`. The footer uses `<h2>` for link groups (Product, Docs…) on every custom page, and `<script type="module">` is emitted after `</html>` on the home page. - **Social tags.** `og:type=article` is used on listing pages (blog index, suites, 404). There is no `twitter:image:alt` or `og:image:width/height`, no `article:published_time` on blog posts, and no `apple-touch-icon`. `<meta name="keywords">` on test pages is ignored by Google; drop it. - **Fonts.** There is no `<link rel="preload">` for the latin Inter and Geist Mono woff2, which are discovered late through the CSS. Font-display is `swap`. Self-hosted, 10 woff plus 13 woff2 files are shipped, but only the matching subsets download. - **Contrast.** In dark mode, `--sl-color-gray-4` (#71717a) on #18181b is 3.7:1, which fails AA for text. It is only defined for borders and Docusaurus-compat variables. Other pairs checked pass: gray-4 on #fafafa is 4.6:1, and the accent is 7.2:1 dark and 5.1:1 light. - **`/docs/tests` is 777 KB HTML (71 KB gzip) with about 1,789 table rows.** It is acceptable, but a large DOM. 20

22	- Multi-tenant rollup: `/tenants` page, tenant list in the sidebar, top-bar switcher, and a Tenants tab on a test. Dev sample `?sample=tenants` (`src/lib/sampleTenants.ts`).

25	
26	**How to apply:** don't implement until Merill rules on the "Decisions for Merill" list in the proposal. Related: [[maester-3-design]], [[maester-marketplace-design]].

Full-page shots are named `<page>-<d|m>-<light|dark>.png`, and the readable crops are in `s/`. Nothing in the repo was edited. I skipped the home hero mock and the explainer video, as asked.
  
  ## CRITICAL
  
  1. **Mobile marketing header has no navigation.**
     - Where: `/`, `/contributors`, `/sponsor`, `/manifesto`, `/test-builder`, `src/layouts/SiteLayout.astro` and `site.css`.
     - What I saw: at 390px the header shows only logo, GitHub icon, theme toggle and Get started (`s/homeheadm.png`, `s/homem-0.png`). Docs, Catalog, Packs, Blog, Contributors and Sponsor are in the DOM but hidden, with no hamburger. A phone user can only reach them through the footer.
     - Fix: add a menu button with a sheet or drawer. Make Docs, Test catalog, Packs and Blog the top level, and keep Sponsor and Cloud there too.
  
  2. **The catalog opens on junk and renders all 888 rows at once.**
     - Where: `/docs/tests`, `TestCatalog`.
     - What I saw: the page is 64,645px tall (`s/tests-0.png`). The first rows are AD-CFG-01 to AD-CFG-14, "…should be retrievable", all Info. That is the first impression of the headline feature.
     - Fix: sort by severity then ID, or show a curated "popular" default. Paginate or virtualise the rows. Show an empty-state and "clear filters" row.
  
  3. **Catalog table is broken on mobile.**
     - What I saw: at 390px only ID and part of CHECK are visible (`s/testsm.png`). Product and severity are clipped with no scroll cue.
     - Fix: below 640px, collapse each row into a card (ID and severity chip, then title, then product).
  
  4. **The install command doesn't match "docs describe the preview".**
     - Where: `/docs/installation` and the hero.
     - What I saw: the installation page, the hero and "Install" step 1 all say `Install-Module Maester` or `-Scope CurrentUser`. The version picker says the default view is the preview, which needs `-AllowPrerelease` (`s/vp.png`). A first-time user following the default docs gets 2.3.0, and MT.1228 and the new parameters then don't exist.
     - Fix: make the install snippet channel-aware (`PreviewOnly` / `Explainer` style) and keep the hero consistent with it.
  
  5. **Manifesto has no title.**
     - Where: `/manifesto` (`s/man-0.png`). It starts straight at the body paragraph with no H1, eyebrow or byline.
     - Fix: add the H1 "The Maester manifesto" and an author line, and set the `<title>`.
  
  ## HIGH
  
  6. **Check counts disagree.**
     - What I saw: the hero says 888 built-in checks. The stats strip and "Browse 1,224 checks" say 1,224. That CTA lands on a catalog that says "Search 888 checks" (`s/home-1.png`, `s/tests-0.png`). The 336 ZTA results aren't in the catalog.
     - Fix: one number everywhere, or make the catalog include ZTA or say why it doesn't.
  
  7. **Catalog controls are unstyled defaults.**
     - What I saw: native `<select>`s, a native checkbox, and ID links in browser-default blue (#0000EE) and underlined (purple when visited in dark mode, `s/testsdk-0.png`). Elsewhere (the CIS page, test pages) links are ember red (`s/cis-0.png`), so the catalog looks unfinished. There are no filter chips, no clear-all, and counts don't update with the other filters. The "Suites" sidebar items don't filter. "TAGS FROM 2.X" is an empty heading. Columns wrap needlessly, so "Active Directory" takes two lines in a 70px row.
     - Fix: use styled combobox or segmented controls with tokenised link colour. Show active-filter chips with a Reset button, make sidebar suites set `?suite=`, and remove the empty group.
  
  8. **Heading scale is too flat and anchors hide under the sticky header.**
     - What I saw: computed sizes are H1 42px, H2 35px, body 16px (`s/intro-0.png`). "Introduction" and "What is Maester?" read as equals, and the H3 "Pre-requisites" under H2 on `/docs/monitoring/github` is almost the same size. `scroll-margin-top` is 0, so jumping to `#anchor` puts the heading under the 96px header.
     - Fix: H1 about 36 and H2 about 24-26 with a top rule or spacing. Add `scroll-margin-top: 112px` to headings in `theme.css`.
  
  9. **Commands: raw PowerShell help, with rendering bugs.**
     - Where: `/docs/commands/*`, `/docs/commands`.
     - What I saw:
       - ALL-CAPS H2s (SYNOPSIS, SYNTAX, DESCRIPTION) and 23 "EXAMPLE n" headings that fill the whole right TOC. Parameters, the useful part, fall below the fold and the TOC is cut off (`s/inv-0.png`).
       - The syntax block is clipped at the right with no scroll affordance.
       - Markdown is mangled in the description: "(Test..ps1) are found … Pester-format custom tests (.Tests.ps1)" shows italics and lost asterisks.
       - The Commands index shows literal `Test.<ID>.ps1` (`s/cmds-0.png`).
       - The description still says "run the Pester tests".
       - The parameter metadata is a coloured code block (`s/invpack.png`).
     - Fix:
       - Add a generator pass: sentence-case headings, collapse examples to "Examples" with captions, and keep only parameters in the TOC.
       - Escape `*` and `<` in help text.
       - Use a compact table for Type, Required, Default and so on.
       - Add a copy button and a wrap toggle on the syntax block.
       - Group the sidebar into Run, Connect, Report, Packs, Authoring and Utility instead of a flat 150-item alphabetical list that wraps long names. "Overview" appears twice.
  
  10. **Test pages lack navigation and a call to action.**
      - Where: `/docs/tests/MT.1001`, `/docs/tests/MT.1228`.
      - What I saw:
        - The 4-line H1 "MT.1228 - Ensure iOS…devices." carries a hyphen and a trailing period (`s/mt1228-0.png`).
        - No breadcrumb (Catalog › Intune › Device compliance), no back link, no prev/next, and no "Run this check" snippet such as `Invoke-Maester -TestId MT.1228`.
        - The sidebar doesn't highlight the suite.
        - The chips duplicate the metadata table at the bottom, which shows raw values (`nist-800-53-r5:SI-7`, `INTUNE_A`, "Supports controls").
        - MT.1001's remediation is placeholder text: "Review the configuration described above."
        - The byline is a 20px avatar plus a sentence. Co-contributors are a count, not names.
      - Fix:
        - Add a breadcrumb and a compact meta block at the top: severity, product, suite and frameworks (CIS/CISA/NIST as chips that link to the catalog filter), a run command with copy, and an edit-on-GitHub link.
        - Show the title in sentence case without "ID -", with the ID as an eyebrow.
        - Humanise license SKUs.
        - Put the Test Metadata table in a collapsed "Details".
        - Put the "Only in the preview" box below the title, in one line.
  
  11. **The 2.x docs are mislabelled.**
      - Where: `/docs/2.x/intro` (`s/v2-0.png`).
      - What I saw: the sidebar has a stray top-level group labelled "0" with a nested duplicate tree. The picker still says "3.0 preview", and nothing says you're reading archived 2.x. The tabs (Catalog, Commands, Packs) jump to 3.0 content.
      - Fix: set the picker to "2.x (archived)", add a banner with a "go to current" link, and fix the sidebar generation.

      - Where: `/test-builder`, `/eidsca-sync`, `/sponsor`.
      - What I saw: the header and home sections use a 1168px container, but these pages are full-bleed at 16px (`s/tb-0.png`, `s/eid-0.png`). The Sponsor "For organisations" card spans the full viewport (`s/sp-0.png`). EIDSCA sync has a default grey `<button>`, centred table headers and unstyled tables. These pages are also not in the nav.
      - Fix: wrap them in the `SiteLayout` container with a max width (about 1120 or 880 for prose) and use the shared button and table classes. Mark `/eidsca-sync` as noindex or move it to the maintainer docs.
  
  13. **Sponsor logos are clipped and broken.**
      - What I saw: on `/sponsor` the CyberDrain logo shows as "yberDrain" and the Increment logo overflows and overlaps its twin (`s/sp-0.png`). On the home Sponsors block the logo tiles are empty boxes, with a "BACKERS" label above nothing (`s/home-5.png`).

The marketing header (`s/home-0.png`) has none of search, version or tabs. The label "Docs" on one side is "Guides" on the other. The logo is smaller in docs.

      - What I saw: the drawer holds the tabs and sidebar (`s/mobmenu.png`), but the version picker, Sponsor, theme and Copy page aren't reachable on phones. The MT.1228 preview box cuts off `-AllowPrerelease -Force` (`s/mt1228m-0.png`).

content.content:
label: AD Connection Troubleshooting
  order: 3
---
## Overview
- Maester uses System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapConnection for cross-platform AD connectivity.
- TLS is required for all AD connections.
## Understanding TLS Modes
- The -ActiveDirectoryTlsMode parameter supports three values: Auto, Ldaps, StartTls.
- Auto (default): Tries LDAPS (port 636) first, then StartTLS (port 389) on Windows. On Linux/macOS, only tries LDAPS.
- Ldaps: Uses LDAPS on port 636 only.
- StartTls: Uses StartTLS on port 389 only.
- Auto mode adapts to the platform due to a known .NET limitation.
## Certificate Issues on the Domain Controller
- Common symptoms: connection fails with certificate, trust, validation, expired, or chain errors.
- Troubleshooting steps:
9:## Overview
13:## Understanding TLS Modes
20:## Certificate Issues on the Domain Controller
30:## Linux and macOS StartTLS Limitation
36:## Using Verbose Output for Diagnostics
45:## Forcing a Specific TLS Mode

cd /Users/merill/github/maester/.claude/worktrees/website-astro; cat > website/scripts/narration/README.md <<'EOF'
# Explainer voice-over and music

Tools for the audio of the website's explainers (`website/public/explainers/<slug>/`). They are not part of the site
build and CI never installs them.

```shell
cd website/scripts/narration
npm install
node narrate.mjs how-it-works   # Kokoro voice-over from the chapters in src/data/explainers.json
node music.mjs how-it-works     # an original music bed, mixed under the voice into audio/mix.mp3
```

- `narrate.mjs` reads each chapter's `say` text (or `text`) and voice from `src/data/explainers.json`, records it with
  [Kokoro](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M) (Apache 2.0; the first run downloads the model, about 330 MB),
  and writes the chapter start times back into `explainers.json` and the composition's `timings.js`.
- `music.mjs` synthesises the music in code (no samples or third-party audio, so there is nothing to license), and
  ducks it while the voice speaks.
- Spell names the way they sound in `say`: "Mayster" for Maester, "Microsoft three sixty-five", "C.I.S.", "Sissa".
EOF
pwsh -NoProfile -Command '
Import-Module Pester -MinimumVersion 5.7.1
$c = New-PesterConfiguration
$c.Run.Path = @("./powershell/tests/general/RepositoryLayout.Tests.ps1","./powershell/tests/general/AgentFiles.Tests.ps1","./powershell/tests/general/TestBuilderData.Tests.ps1","./powershell/tests/functions/engine/Frameworks.Tests.ps1")
$c.Output.Verbosity = "None"; $c.Run.PassThru = $true
$r = Invoke-Pester -Configuration $c
"Passed: $($r.PassedCount) Failed: $($r.FailedCount)"; $r.Failed | ForEach-Object { $_.ExpandedPath }' 2>&1 | tail -5

lines:
"Feature": "The part of the product the test is about. One key from the product's `Features` list.

- Choose the feature whose settings page or object type the remediation sends the admin to.
- When a test spans two features, choose the one that fails most directly. A Conditional Access policy that
  requires a compliant device is `conditional-access`, not `devices`.
- Tests that check the same thing get the same feature, whatever folder or suite they are in.
- A feature that would hold one test only is usually too narrow. Prefer an existing feature.",

"Area": "The security theme, whatever the product. One key.

| Key | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `authentication` | How an identity proves who it is: MFA, authentication methods, passwords, legacy protocols, Kerberos and NTLM hardening, session and token lifetime. |
| `privileged-access` | Administrative roles and accounts: who holds them, just-in-time elevation, emergency access, admin tiering, delegated admin rights. |
| `access-control` | Who may reach which resource under which conditions: device, location and risk conditions, permissions on objects, user defaults. |
| `applications` | App registrations, service principals and their credentials, consent and API permissions, OAuth apps, add-ins, connectors. |
| `external-access` | Guests, cross-tenant access, federation and trusts, external sharing and external communication. |
| `devices` | Device compliance, enrollment and configuration, endpoint protection, device identity. |
| `email-protection` | Anti-phishing, anti-spam and anti-malware, Safe Links and Safe Attachments, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, mail flow rules, meeting and messaging protections. |
| `data-protection` | Data loss prevention, sensitivity labels, encryption, retention, backup. |
| `logging-and-detection` | Audit logs, diagnostic settings, alert policies, sensors and the health of detection tooling. |
| `identity-lifecycle` | Stale and dormant accounts, ownership, access reviews, entitlement management, group membership hygiene. |
| `infrastructure` | The directory and platform itself: domain controllers, DNS, replication, sites, schema, Group Policy health, protocol hardening, subscriptions, tenant-wide platform settings. |
| `engineering-systems` | DevOps organizations, repositories, pipelines, build identities, the software supply chain. |
| `ai` | AI agents and copilots: who can use and share them, how they authenticate, what data and tools they reach. |

When more than one area fits, choose by what the control is for, in this order:

1. It protects administrators or admin rights: `privileged-access`.
2. It decides how sign-in is proven: `authentication`.
3. It is about an application, service principal or agent as the subject: `applications`, or `ai` for agents.
4. It is about people or data outside the organization: `external-access`.
